## Summary

I changed the `customerCode` format from `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` to `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`.

**`AssignCustomerCode.java`** — the one place that builds the code:
- Now derives a `CITY3` segment (upper-cased first three letters of the city) alongside the existing `LAST3` segment, factored into a shared `prefix(...)` helper so the two segments don't duplicate substring/upper-case logic.
- The `NNNN` sequence is now **per-city**: it counts existing owners in the same city (case-insensitive, following the established `findAll()`-and-fold pattern used by `AssignNamesakeCount`) and uses one more than that count, instead of the previous global owner count.

**`AssignMembershipNumber.java`** — the only value derived from `customerCode`. Its logic already reads `owner.getCustomerCode()` dynamically, so the membership number is automatically rebuilt on the new format (e.g. `LON-SMI-0007-M26`); I only updated its Javadoc example to match.

The new `AcceptanceTest.coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix` (asserting the `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}` shape) passes, and the full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 0 failures/errors).
